    Virtual trialsfor realpatients.

    A pharmacogenomic simulator for antiplatelet therapy in Indian populations. Every point in the scene is a virtual patient, built from published genotype frequencies and run through a published pharmacology model.

    CYP2C19
    The liver enzyme that converts clopidogrel into its active form. Common gene variants weaken it; one variant, *17, increases it.
    Metaboliser
    A patient's CYP2C19 category, set by the two gene copies they carry: ultrarapid, rapid, normal, intermediate or poor.
    PRU
    P2Y12 reaction units, a blood test of how reactive platelets remain on treatment. Above 208 PRU counts as high on-treatment reactivity.
    — of this virtual cohort stays above 208 PRU at 75 mg a day
    75 mg
    Standard maintenance is 75 mg. Each step is a separate engine run on the same patients.

    02The question

    What does a standard clopidogrel dose actually do in an Indian population?

    Clopidogrel is widely prescribed after a heart attack and stenting, yet it only works once CYP2C19 converts it to its active form. Variants that impair that enzyme are far more common in South Asians than in the European populations most dosing evidence comes from. This tool builds virtual patients from published allele frequencies, runs a published pharmacokinetic–pharmacodynamic model on them, and reports what a standard dose leaves behind, then asks what it would cost to do something about it.

    Out of every 100 virtual patients on 75 mg a daystored from 20,000-patient build runs
    above 208 PRUat or below
    What is computed where. Figures on this page carry one of two tags. computed in this browser means the simulation engine on this page produced it: the cohort, the mechanism, your own trial runs, the single-patient explorer, the population histograms, and the trial-design and economics read-outs. stored from build means it was computed when this page was built and is stored in it, such as the population table and the validation results. Parameter values and citations in Provenance are transcribed from their published sources. No patient data is used, and nothing you enter leaves this page.
    The gradient this tool exists to quantifystored from build runs

    What this is

    • A virtual cohort generator. Genotypes are drawn under Hardy–Weinberg from published CYP2C19 allele frequencies for named populations, then mapped to phenotype by the CPIC 2022 rules.
    • A reimplementation of a published popPK-PD model (Jung 2024), with one transparently fitted calibration parameter and a validation section showing every check it passes and fails.
    • A decision layer: how many patients an Indian confirmatory trial would need, and what genotyping would cost per event averted, in rupees.
    • Fully sourced. Every number in the Provenance chapter carries its citation and a label saying whether we read the primary source, a secondary report, derived it, or assumed it.

    What this is not

    • Not clinical evidence. It cannot recommend treatment for an individual patient, and no output should be read as doing so.
    • Not a claim that genotyping prevents events. TAILOR-PCI reported a hazard ratio of 0.66 with a confidence interval of 0.43 to 1.02 and p = 0.06. It did not meet significance.
    • Not an AI that discovered anything. The neural network here reproduces this tool's own model quickly. It learned no biology.
    • Not first. PharmCAT and CPIC already interpret a genotype, and an open-source clopidogrel PBPK model already exists in PK-Sim. The Limits chapter names them and states what is left over.
    In plain words

    Gene variants that blunt clopidogrel are common in South Asians, while most of the dosing evidence was gathered in other populations.

    How to read this honestly

    The network cannot be more correct than the model that produced its training labels, and its errors add to that model's own. Attribution explains the surrogate's behaviour, and because every input here is one you set, it functions as a consistency check that the model responds the way the pharmacology says it should, not as a method for discovering anything.

    In plain words

    The genes a patient inherits set how much clopidogrel they activate, and that largely decides whether their platelets stay too reactive.

    04Populations

    The same dose, different populations

    Each population is an independent virtual trial at 75 mg once daily, differing only in the published allele frequencies the cohort was drawn from. This is the comparison the tool exists to make, and the caveat it comes with sits directly under the table.

    Distribution of on-treatment reactivity, four reference populationscomputed in this browser, 4,000 patients each
    All populations at a standard dosestored from build runs
    Read this table with its limitation attached. The South Asian panels in the 1000 Genomes reference are roughly hundred-person diaspora cohorts: only the Indian Telugu and Gujarati Indian panels are India-origin, and Punjabi Lahore, Bengali Bangladesh and Sri Lankan Tamil are not. They are not a regionally stratified survey of India, and published Indian estimates of *2 frequency themselves span roughly 27% to 41%. The *2 frequency control in your own trial run exists so you can vary that frequency rather than trust one point estimate.
    In plain words

    The same dose leaves more South and East Asian virtual patients under-treated than European ones, but the Indian genetic data behind that comes from small panels.

    05Trial design

    How large would an Indian confirmatory trial have to be?

    The simulated event rates feed a two-proportion sample-size calculation, so the cohort's genotype composition determines how many patients would have to be screened to randomise enough carriers. The first thing this reveals is why the one large trial that tried this came out at p = 0.06.

    Power against total randomisedcomputed in this browser
    Against the trial that was actually run
    One caution about what this calculation can and cannot tell you. The treatment effect it assumes comes from a meta-analysis of switching loss-of-function carriers to a more potent agent, and the baseline event rate comes from non-Indian trial arms, because no verified twelve-month event rate from an Indian post-PCI cohort on clopidogrel was found. Change the baseline rate control and watch the required sample size move sharply: that sensitivity is the honest headline, not the point estimate.
    In plain words

    Settling this question in India would take a trial of thousands of patients; on these assumptions the one large trial so far was too small to give a clear answer.

    06Economics

    What would it cost, and would India buy it?

    Costs are in rupees and no figure here is converted from another currency. The threshold is the empirical Indian willingness-to-pay estimate rather than a generic multiple of per-capita income. The answer at today's prices is no, and the useful part is seeing exactly what would have to change.

    Height is net monetary benefit per patient: what the QALYs gained are worth at the Indian threshold, minus what the strategy costs. The traced line is where that reaches zero, which is the cost-effectiveness frontier itself. Net benefit is used rather than cost per QALY because it stays linear in both prices and has no singularity where incremental cost crosses zero. The brass marker follows the two price controls below.

    Cost per patient over twelve months

    Each bar spans the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio across the plausible range of one input, holding the rest at their current settings. The dashed line is the willingness-to-pay threshold.

    In plain words

    At today's Indian prices, testing and switching costs far more per healthy year gained than India's threshold, and the price of the alternative drug, not the test, is the main barrier.

            10Summary

            What this shows, and what it does not

            • It shows a gap

              At a standard dose, a larger share of a virtual South Asian cohort stays above the 208 PRU line than a European one, because no-function CYP2C19 alleles are more common.

            • It shows what testing would take

              A confirmatory Indian trial would need thousands of patients, and at today's prices genotype-guided switching is not cost-effective against India's threshold. The alternative drug's price is the binding constraint.

            • It does not show benefit

              It never claims that genotype-guided therapy reduces events. It is not clinical evidence and cannot recommend treatment for an individual patient. It is meant for education and for identifying where prospective Indian studies and genotype testing matter most.

            ANUKRITI

            अनुकृति, Sanskrit for simulation or imitation. An in-silico pharmacogenomic trial simulator for antiplatelet therapy in Indian populations.
